newsitem.title: USA: U.S. WCoast crudes gain modestly in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. WCoast crudes gain modestly in late trade.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes edged up late Friday on the back of modest rises in bellwether West Texas Intermediate, while diffs stayed flat.
Spot October WTI traded around $22.20/22.30 a barrel late Friday, up five cents from earlier levels.
NYMEX futures markets will be closed Monday in observance of the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
With supplies long and refiners evaluating their September needs, players had little to discuss with one another.

But buyers saw the flush stocks of West Coast crudes lowering deltas. One refinery was planning to offer Alaska North Slope crude at $2.20 a barrel under October WTI, which was last trade at $2.05 under.
Texaco bought around 500,000 barrels of light sour Canadian crude Thursday, according to an industry source.
The "distressed" sale was caused by excess crude backed up from autumn maintenance on a major Canadian pipeline.
Kern River prices were idle at $14/14.50 a barrel.
Wilmington also stagnated at 16.10/16.20 a barrel.
Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel, with little trading seen ahead of mid-September.
